chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Maskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
«Cruel, moreover, a bastard.» He said: The great cruelty is disbelief, and the villainous is the one who wantons with his disbelief.

key_terms.الزَّنِيمُ: The villainous or one who is heedless/arrogant
key_terms.الْعَتَلُ: The cruel or severe in punishment/disbelief
key_terms.الْمُسْتَهْتِرُ: The one who is heedless or treats something lightly

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Al-'atal' and 'Az-zanim' in Surah Al-Qalam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this exegetical tradition to clarify the specific attributes of the disbelievers of Makkah mentioned in Surah Al-Qalam, linking linguistic nuance to theological state. It defines 'Al-'atal' as the magnitude of disbelief itself, while 'Az-zanim' characterizes the individual's arrogant and heedless attitude toward that disbelief, a distinction often cited in Shia tafsir to highlight the severity of their spiritual condition.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Isa, from Abbas bin Ma’ruf, from Safwan bin Yahya, from Ibn Maskan, from Muhammed bin Muslim, that he said: I said to Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him:
«Cruel, moreover, a bastard.» [68:13] He said: The great cruelty is disbelief, and the villainous is the one who wantons with his disbelief.
